key_factors: Hugo Broos' 4-2-3-1 designed for defensive compactness and counter-attacking
South Africa train at Johannesburg altitude (~1,753m) — better acclimatised than pure sea-level nations
Lyle Foster (€10.3M) is a genuine counter-attack threat behind Mexico's high defensive line
Ronwen Williams — experienced goalkeeper, kept clean sheet vs Nicaragua
Mokoena/Adams double pivot can limit Mexico's midfield control
RSA will be organised and competitive for at least 60 minutes
reasoning: Bafana Bafana are realistically underdogs here. Mexico's home advantage at altitude is the dominant factor. However, South Africa's domestic altitude experience is a genuine mitigant, and Hugo Broos' defensive structure should keep this competitive through the first hour. We believe Foster will punish one defensive mistake on the counter. Mexico's quality tells in the end, but Bafana will not leave empty-handed in terms of spirit. Prediction: Mexico 2-1 South Africa — a defeat, but one where Bafana showed they belong.
